4: TBP recognises the ATA box (−30) and Mediator links you to the erythroid activators (KLF1, GATA1) and to the LCR.
5: TFIID (TBP on CATAAA, DNA bent by ≈ 80°), TFIIA, TFIIB (sets +1), Pol II–TFIIF, TFIIE, TFIIH. KLF1 (CACCC), NF-Y (CCAAT) and the LCR (GATA1/TAL1/LDB1) act through Mediator.
6: Classic variants here: c.92+1G>A (β⁰), c.92+5G>C and c.92+6T>C (β⁺).
7: The variant c.93-21G>A (IVS1-110) creates a cryptic AG here.
8: Classic variants: c.315+1G>A (β⁰), c.316-197C>T (IVS2-654) and c.316-106C>G (IVS2-745), which activate cryptic sites.
9: The variant c.*110T>C (AAUAAA → AACAAA) abolishes this signal: β⁺-thalassaemia.
10: On HBB, which is very highly transcribed, re-initiation is helped by the complex left on the promoter and by the LCR–promoter loop.
17: ATA box (CATAAA, −30); STAT3 site (TTCTTGGAA, −93, orange bead) responding to interleukin 6: this is the anaemia of inflammation; BMP response element (GGCGCC, −105, purple bead) binding SMAD1/5/8–SMAD4 when BMP6, secreted by the sinusoidal endothelium according to iron stores, activates its receptor and the co-receptor haemojuvelin. Transferrin saturation, sensed by HFE and TFR2, strengthens this signal; erythroferrone from erythroblasts dampens it.
19: A second BMP response element (BMP-RE2), ≈ 2.3 kb upstream, cooperates with the proximal site: the loop brings the SMADs bound there, with neighbouring hepatic factors, close to the promoter.
21: Transcribed but not translated. The ribosome scans from the cap to the first AUG.
23: Three exons, 84 codons: preprohepcidin. The signal peptide (24 amino acids) is removed in the ER, then furin cuts after the RRRRR motif and releases hepcidin-25 (DTHFPICIFCCGCCHRSKCGMCCKT), folded into a hairpin by 4 disulfide bonds. It binds ferroportin, plugs it and triggers its internalisation: iron stays in enterocytes and macrophages. Pink markers: juvenile haemochromatosis variants.
26: Contains the polyadenylation signal AATAAA, about thirty nucleotides before the cleavage site.
28: 7-methylguanosine cap + CBC complex (white) from 25 nt. Gold exons, blue introns (the first is 2.1 kb), green poly(A) tail added after cleavage by CPSF. Splicing is co-transcriptional.
30: Mature mRNA: 406 nt + poly(A), compacted with CBC, EJC and PABPN1. The TREX complex recruits the export receptor NXF1–NXT1; through the pore, cap first. Follow it!
32: As soon as the signal peptide emerges from the ribosome, the SRP particle pauses translation and docks the ribosome onto the Sec61 translocon of the outer nuclear membrane, which is rough ER. The 84-amino-acid chain enters the lumen; the hepatocyte will secrete hepcidin-25 into sinusoidal blood (red dot = nascent chain).
34: Irregularly shaped condensate (20 to 50 per nucleus) made of 20–25 nm interchromatin granules. At the core (pink): the proteins SON and SRRM2, without which it dissolves. Around them: SR proteins (cyan) and snRNPs (blue). At the periphery: the long non-coding RNA MALAT1 (orange). No DNA and no transcription inside: it is a reserve of splicing factors in constant exchange with the nucleoplasm. Genes sitting against it are spliced more efficiently — here HAMP.
35: TBP recognises the ATA box (−30). Just upstream, SMAD (iron signal, via BMP6) and STAT3 (inflammation signal, via IL-6) set the output: you are transcribing the gene of the iron hormone.
36: TFIID (TBP on CATAAA), TFIIA, TFIIB, Pol II–TFIIF, TFIIE, TFIIH. SMAD1/5/8–SMAD4 on the BMP-RE1 element (GGCGCC, −105) and STAT3 on TTCTTGGAA (−93) recruit p300/CBP and Mediator; the distal BMP-RE2 (−2.3 kb) cooperates.
37: Intron 2 is only 89 nt long, close to the minimal size of a human intron.
40: One of the best understood promoters. TATA box (−33); CRE (TGACG, −64, purple bead) binding CREB, phosphorylated on Ser133 by kinases activated by Ca²⁺ and cAMP; SRE (CCATATTAGG, −314, blue and pink beads) binding SRF and the ternary complex factor ELK1, a target of the Ras–ERK pathway; SIE (−348, orange bead) binding STAT. Before any stimulus, an RNA polymerase II is already engaged and paused: transcription starts within minutes. FOS is the prototype immediate early gene.
42: Five enhancers (e1 to e5) flank the gene. Depending on the stimulus — synaptic activity, BDNF — different combinations switch on, bind CBP and are themselves transcribed into enhancer RNA (eRNA). Looping brings them to the promoter.
45: Four exons, 380 codons: c-Fos. Exons 3 and 4 encode the bZIP domain — a basic region that reads DNA, then a leucine zipper. c-Fos does not homodimerise: paired with JUN it forms the AP-1 factor, which binds TGA(C/G)TCA sites and launches the second wave of activity-response genes (synaptic plasticity, memory).
48: Rich in AU elements (AUUUA motifs) that recruit the deadenylation and decay machinery: FOS mRNA lives only about fifteen minutes, which makes the response transient. AATAAA polyadenylation signal near the end.
50: 7-methylguanosine cap + CBC complex (white) from 25 nt. Gold exons, blue introns, green poly(A) tail added after cleavage by CPSF. Splicing is co-transcriptional. Detectable a few minutes after a burst of synaptic activity: it is used to map active neurons.
51: Mature mRNA: 2,104 nt + poly(A), compacted with CBC, EJC and PABPN1. The TREX complex recruits the export receptor NXF1–NXT1; through the pore, cap first. Follow it!
53: The mRNA is translated in the cytosol (380 amino acids; red dot = nascent chain). c-Fos carries a nuclear localisation signal: importins bring it back into the nucleus, where it pairs with JUN to form AP-1. Protein and mRNA are unstable: the peak lasts only one to two hours.
54: Irregularly shaped condensate (20 to 50 per nucleus) made of 20–25 nm interchromatin granules. At the core (pink): the proteins SON and SRRM2, without which it dissolves. Around them: SR proteins (cyan) and snRNPs (blue). At the periphery: the long non-coding RNA MALAT1 (orange). No DNA and no transcription inside: it is a reserve of splicing factors in constant exchange with the nucleoplasm. Genes sitting against it are spliced more efficiently — here FOS.
